transcription.text: Lightning is close. Who tells the crew to stop? The cabinet lights and sounder first.
This page is the backup. The top line says it too. WakeCap lightning alerts are a backup.
Always follow the site's cabinet lights and sounder first. The state tile read all clear
when we captured this. WakeCap treats only the green state as safe to work. The rings and chips
are the configured alert distances. The page says so plainly, zone reference only, not a live strike
position. New here, a map of the alert distances. Its legend reads a red ring, a yellow ring, and a
dot for the sensor. Below, a new alarm activity chart counts yellow and red alarms. In this window,
both read zero. No alarms were raised in this window. Export CSV is grayed out. Times are
Saudi time. For a site screenshot,
a wallboard view. The same state, large, with the backup line beneath it. And a phone width view.
Both open by address, a web address, not from the menu. Where does that state come from? A small
input module reads the sensor. On the wireless mesh, it shows up as a Modbus device. Modbus is
an industrial wiring and data standard, many sensors speak. A gateway passes the readings
to the cloud, then to this page, and anything unreadable is set aside.
In the menu, you can open Settings, then Lightning. It needs its own permission,
apart from viewing. These are the alert distances the tile shows as rings. Two buttons,
edit alerting radii, and set location. The location is entered by hand, marked temporary.
Below that, a 24-hour state history. Green rows, with data unavailable rows between.
The page shows the gaps instead of hiding them. New on this page, a map of the alert distances,
an alarm chart and history, and lightning settings. Back to the crew. Next step. If your
project has lightning, open it and read the banner at the top. Cabinet lights and sounder first.
